extraction.name: FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We start with the FLoRes-101 dataset. FLoRes-101 contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and these sentences have been translated in 101 languages by human translators. Because the test set of FLoRes-101 is not publicly available, we only use the dev and devtest sets, which contain 2009 sentences in total. We split those sentences into new train, dev and test splits, with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences respectively. For each sentence in the 102 languages (101 counted in FLoRes plus English), we collected three recordings by three different native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. We plan to fill these gaps in the future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes-101 dataset containing 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia that have been translated in 101 languages by human translators. We only use the dev and devtest sets, which contain 2009 sentences in total.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We split the collected data into train, development (dev) and test sets with disjoint speakers between train/dev and test, with a target ratio of 7:1:2. All the segments are within 30 seconds.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For source transcripts, we reuse the transcripts produced by human translators from FLoRes-101. We apply NFC and then FST normalization to each sentence, lower-case, normalize and remove punctuations. We also split words into characters, and define the token as word boundaries. For each sentence, three versions are provided: the original raw transcript (SRC_RAW), the preprocessed version (SRC_NORM) and its character-based version (SRC_CHAR), which should be used for ASR. All recordings are kept as they-are, either from quiet or noisy environment, without any data augmentations (e.g: SpecAugment, speed perturbation, simulated reverberation, etc.). The speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After the first recording step, each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assesses whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded, leaving us between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings by three different native speakers per sentence, with validation by additional workers
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers with a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. We plan to fill these gaps in the future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Sex ratio of speakers (at least 30/70% balance when possible), native speaker status, language
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding. With FLEURS, we hope to provide a resource that could catalyze research towards building massively multilingual speech and text representations and their evaluation on a variety of tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. Results are much better on the Western European group than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli. Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction for future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS is well-suited for several downstream tasks including ASR, Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech LangID, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval. Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning.
